seo.title: Park Hyatt Mallorca: 5-Star Canyamel Honeymoon Review (2026)
seo.description: Hilltop Tramuntana-style hamlet above Canyamel cove. 142 keys, three pools, Serenitas spa, 2 Michelin stars next door. Honest 2026 verdict, real cost, best room, 7-night itinerary.

content.verdict: Park Hyatt Mallorca is the island's most ambitious resort opening of the last decade — a 142-key hilltop village above Canyamel cove on the east coast, designed by Madrid architects RCR-Aranguren as a stylised Tramuntana hamlet of honey-stone houses, bell-tower lobby, and three cascading pools that step down towards the Mediterranean. Set inside a 1,200-hectare estate that includes the Canyamel Pueblo Golf course and a Roman tower from the 13th century, the property combines the polished Park Hyatt service standard with a genuine sense of place — quieter and less scene-y than Cap Rocat, more architecturally serious than any other resort on the island's east coast, and with the rare advantage of two Michelin stars (Voro by Álvaro Salazar) on-site. For couples who want resort-scale facilities — multiple pools, full spa, two restaurants and three bars, a Posidonia-meadow private beach club a short shuttle away — combined with east-coast quiet and proper Mediterranean architecture, this is the Mallorca address.
content.best_room: A King Park Suite Sea View on the upper village terraces is the honeymoon room — 75 sqm with a separate sitting area, a deep stone soaking tub, and a private terrace facing east over the Mediterranean for unforgettable sunrise coffee. For the most romantic stay, the Presidential Suite occupies its own tower-house at the village edge with a private plunge pool, outdoor dining terrace, and uninterrupted sea views. Avoid the standard Park Rooms on the lower terraces — they face the central plaza rather than the sea and lose the resort's defining view.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Arrival at Canyamel
itinerary_7_nights.description: Fly into Palma (PMI) and transfer 70 minutes east to Canyamel — the drive across the central plain past Llucmajor's windmills sets the tone. Settle into your Park Suite, swim a slow afternoon length in the cascading central pool, and book the rooftop Asia restaurant for first-night cocktails as the bell tower lights up.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Beach Club & Spa Day
itinerary_7_nights.description: Morning shuttle (5 minutes) to the hotel's private beach club at Cala Canyamel — a calm horseshoe cove with white sand, Posidonia-meadow snorkelling, and a casual beachfront kitchen. Afternoon at Serenitas Spa for the signature 90-minute couples treatment in the candlelit hammam suite, followed by sunset dinner at Voro (book the tasting menu — 14 courses around Salazar's two-star Mediterranean kitchen).

itinerary_7_nights.title: Caves of Drach & Porto Cristo
itinerary_7_nights.description: Drive 25 minutes south to the Cuevas del Drach — Mallorca's most famous limestone caves with their underground Lake Martel and the daily classical-music boat performance. Lunch in nearby Porto Cristo at Ses Comes for fresh red mullet, then return via Cala Mesquida for an afternoon swim on the island's most photogenic sandy bay.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Cap de Formentor
itinerary_7_nights.description: A full day north to Cap de Formentor — the island's dramatic northern lighthouse cape with the Mirador Es Colomer cliff viewpoint and the iconic switchback road past Cala Figuera. Lunch at the legendary Hotel Formentor (recently reopened as Four Seasons) and an afternoon swim in Cala Pi de la Posada before the 90-minute drive back to Canyamel for dinner at the village's plaza restaurant Tomeu.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Tramuntana Mountain Villages
itinerary_7_nights.description: An hour west to the Tramuntana — Valldemossa for Chopin's monastery, Deià for the cliff-edge village walk and lunch at El Olivo (the Belmond La Residencia restaurant), and a late-afternoon stop in Sóller for the historic wooden tram down to Port de Sóller. The contrast with Canyamel's gentle east coast is striking.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Boat Day along the East Coast
itinerary_7_nights.description: Charter a private gulet from Cala Ratjada (15 minutes north) for a full day along the protected east coast — Cala Mondragó's twin coves, Cala Varques, and the offshore island of Cabrera if the wind allows. Lunch on board, snorkel the Posidonia meadows, and return for a long aperitivo at the Park Hyatt's rooftop Asia bar.

itinerary_7_nights.title: Pool Morning & Departure
itinerary_7_nights.description: A final morning at the cascading infinity pool, breakfast on the terrace, and the 70-minute transfer to Palma. Canyamel is the calmest corner of Mallorca — most guests leave already planning a return.

caveats: Canyamel is genuinely east-coast remote — Palma is 70 minutes away and the Tramuntana mountains require a 90-minute drive. Couples who want easy access to Palma's city life and Deià should consider Cap Rocat or a Tramuntana hotel instead.

Park Hyatt Mallorca welcomes families and runs a Camp Hyatt kids programme; while the resort is large enough to absorb children gracefully, it is not adults-only and peak summer weeks see family bookings.
The on-site beach is a 5-minute shuttle ride rather than direct walking access — minor but worth knowing for guests expecting beach-from-room access.

faqs.question: Good for honeymooners?
faqs.answer: Yes — particularly couples who want full resort facilities (three pools, full spa, Michelin dining on-site) combined with the east coast's quiet and proper Mediterranean architecture. Honeymoon packages include a sparkling-wine welcome, in-suite spa amenities, and a private dinner option at the Roman tower for an additional fee.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: May–June and September–early October are ideal — water above 22°C, evenings warm enough for outdoor dining, and the Tramuntana cool enough for hiking. The hotel closes briefly mid-November to mid-February; April and late October are open but cooler.

faqs.question: Book in advance?
faqs.answer: Park Suite Sea View categories book 3–4 months ahead for July and August; the Presidential Suite needs 6–8 months. Shoulder season (May, September) often has availability within a month.

faqs.question: Adults-only?
faqs.answer: No — Park Hyatt Mallorca is a full-service family-friendly resort. The size of the property (142 keys across a village footprint) means couples can easily find quiet corners, but guests seeking adults-only should consider Castell Son Claret or Belmond La Residencia.

faqs.question: Best room type?
faqs.answer: King Park Suite Sea View on the upper terraces — 75 sqm with a stone soaking tub and east-facing terrace for sunrise. For ultimate honeymoon splurge, the Presidential Suite has its own tower-house with plunge pool and private outdoor dining.

faqs.question: How to get there?
faqs.answer: Palma de Mallorca (PMI) is the only airport — 70 minutes by car to Canyamel. Direct flights from London (2h 15m), Paris (2h), Madrid (1h 15m), Barcelona (50m), Berlin, Munich, Zurich. The hotel arranges private transfers for around €180 one-way.
